class.name: ResourceImporterDirectStorageTexture
class.brief_description: Imports an image for use as a DirectStorage compressed texture ([DSTex]).
class.description: This importer imports [DSTex] ([code].dstex[/code]) compressed texture resources for DirectStorage-accelerated streaming. Image files ([code].png[/code], [code].jpg[/code], [code].jpeg[/code], [code].webp[/code]) are processed with optional S3TC block compression and compressed using Microsoft GDeflate. During export, [EditorExportPlugin] bundles [code].dstex[/code] resources into [code]res://textures.dspkg[/code] via [DSPkg], allowing [DSResourceFormatLoader] and [DSContext] to stream textures directly to GPU or CPU memory at runtime. See also [ResourceImporterTexture], [DSTex], and [DSContext].

members.member: The Microsoft GDeflate compression level applied to the texture data payload in the generated [code].dstex[/code] file, ranging from [code]1[/code] through [code]12[/code]. Lower values (such as the default [code]1[/code]) maximize encoding speed in the editor and provide the highest DirectStorage decompression throughput. Higher values achieve smaller file sizes on disk at the cost of slower import times and increased decompression workload.

The compression mode to use for the imported texture. [b]VRAM Compressed (S3TC):[/b] Compresses texture mipmaps using S3TC block compression (BC1/DXT1 for opaque images, BC3/DXT5 for images with transparency or normal maps) prior to GDeflate compression. This significantly reduces GPU VRAM consumption and optimizes streaming bandwidth. Recommended for standard 3D and 2D textures. [b]VRAM Uncompressed:[/b] Retains uncompressed raw pixel data (such as RGBA8) with mipmaps, compressed only on disk using lossless GDeflate. Preserves perfect pixel fidelity with zero block compression artifacts (ideal for pixel art, crisp UI elements, or lookup tables), but requires significantly more VRAM at runtime.

Controls the source color space and channel interpretation during S3TC block compression: [b]Generic:[/b] Generic linear data texture (such as roughness, metallic, masks, or lookup tables). Color channel distances are evaluated linearly without assuming sRGB gamma encoding. [b]sRGB:[/b] Standard color texture (such as albedo or diffuse maps). Color distances are weighted according to perceptual human vision in sRGB space. [b]Normal Map:[/b] Tangent-space normal map. Red and green channels are prioritized to minimize normal vector distortion and lighting artifacts.

Forces the texture to load into CPU memory as an [ImageTexture] even when GPU streaming prewarm ([method DSPreloader.prewarm_gpu_async]) is active. [b]Note:[/b] Standard runtime loads ([ResourceLoader]) and CPU prewarm ([method DSPreloader.prewarm_async]) already create [ImageTexture] resources automatically. This setting is specifically needed for projects using D3D12 GPU prewarm when an asset requires CPU pixel access—such as [Light3D] projectors ([member Light3D.light_projector]), [Decal] textures, or scripts calling [method Texture2D.get_image]—preventing engine atlas warnings and readback stalls. [b]Note:[/b] Some formats never take the GPU prewarm path regardless of this setting: uncompressed and float data formats (R8, RG8, RGB8, the R16 family, float formats, BC6H) are always prewarmed into [ImageTexture]. Color formats with an sRGB counterpart (BC1, BC2, BC3, BC7, the RGBA8/BGRA8 family) and the linear block formats used by 3D material data (BC4, BC5 - which includes normal maps) do use the GPU path.
